task_instance: Create a minimal Cloudflare Worker project (wrangler.jsonc + src/index.js), install project-local Wrangler via npm, run it locally with `wrangler dev` and verify it serves a real HTTP response, validate the deploy packaging with `wrangler deploy --dry-run`, and generate TypeScript/runtime types with `wrangler types` -- all without touching a real Cloudflare account.
evidence: Created worker-app/ with package.json (devDependency wrangler ^4), wrangler.jsonc (name, main, compatibility_date), and src/index.js returning 'Hello from Worker!'. `npm install` succeeded (added 38 packages, wrangler 4.141.0 installed locally, confirmed via `npx wrangler --version`). `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` succeeded with output 'Total Upload: 0.20 KiB ... No bindings found. --dry-run: exiting now.' -- no authentication was required or prompted. `npx wrangler dev --port 8799` started a local server; `curl http://127.0.0.1:8799/` returned 'Hello from Worker!' confirming the worker actually runs and serves requests locally (log line 'GET / 200 OK'). `npx wrangler types` generated worker-configuration.d.ts (605KB) with Env/runtime types. All commands ran project-locally via npx against the installed lockfile version, matching the skill's guidance to inspect the project and use its local Wrangler rather than a global/newer install. Real `wrangler deploy` to Cloudflare's edge (which requires `wrangler login`/API token and an account) was correctly not attempted, per the safety rules against account-bound/paid services -- this is the expected boundary of the skill for an unauthenticated sandbox, not a failure of the core deliverable (local dev + config authoring + dry-run validation), which was fully achieved and verified.
